print.title: Printer and material
print.chipHint: Change the material of this part and the printer
print.materialFailed: The material could not be set.
print.name: Name
print.printerHint: The highlighted printer is in use. Walls under two line widths print poorly; the assistant is told.
print.materialHint: Starting values, not measured on your printer. Measure them with »Measure tolerances …« on three small test pieces; the assistant designs with these clearances.
print.nameMissing: Every profile needs a name. Until then the last saved profiles stay.
print.saveFailed: The profiles could not be saved.
print.supportFreeHint: The assistant chamfers edges facing the bed instead of rounding them, gives wide lying holes a teardrop roof and bridges countersinks that open downwards, so the slicer needs no support.

design.title: Design well on its own
design.hint: What the assistant adds without being asked. It names it in one line after every step; in the chat you can turn it off for one project ("no fillets"), which goes before these switches. Sizes you name are always built exactly.

rounding.label: Fillets and chamfers
rounding.hint: Visible outer edges rounded 1–3 mm, edges on the bed chamfered, inner corners under load rounded.

printInPlace.label: Print-in-place
printInPlace.hint: Hinges, joints and clips first as one piece that prints ready to use, without assembly or support.

details.label: Details
details.hint: Even walls, chamfered holes and mating edges, sunk screw heads, smooth transitions.

snap.label: Snap sizes
snap.hint: Walls it chooses become whole line widths, floors and heights whole layers. When you change printer, PartBuddy adjusts only these sizes.

print.catalogEmpty: No printer matches. Copy an existing one and enter the values by hand.
print.catalogHint: Values as stated by the maker. It becomes a profile of your own that you can change freely.
print.printersFull: At most {count} printers. Delete one to add another.

materialCatalog.catalogEmpty: No material matches. Copy an existing one and enter the values by hand.
materialCatalog.catalogHint: Starting values per material type from design guides, not measured on your printer. It becomes a profile of your own; adjust it after a test print.

print.materialsFull: At most {count} materials. Delete one to add another.

tolerance.title: Measure tolerances
tolerance.intro: Three small test pieces show which clearances, hole allowance and overhang your printer manages with this material. Only these design values are measured; temperature, flow and the like stay with the slicer.
tolerance.printer: Made for {name}: nozzle {nozzle} mm, layer {layer} mm.
tolerance.pictureAlt: The test pieces: fit comb with pin, hole plate and overhang staircase
tolerance.pieces: A fit comb with a pin, a hole plate with 3, 5, 8 and 10 mm and an overhang staircase from 20° to 70°; every step carries its value.

guide.print: Print with {material} and your usual profile, without supports and without scaling.
guide.noCompensation: Turn off hole and XY compensation in the slicer, or you measure the compensation too.
guide.cool: Let them cool before you measure.

tolerance.working: SolidCraft is building the test pieces …
tolerance.exportFailed: The test pieces could not be made. Is SolidCraft running?
tolerance.comb: Put the pin into the holes and pick for each fit the smallest step that fits.
tolerance.holes: Measure each hole with a caliper. Leave empty what you do not measure.
tolerance.overhang: Steepest step with a clean underside
tolerance.applyHint: Apply writes the values into the material; Save keeps them.

problem.fit: {fit}: not a step of the comb.
problem.hole: Ø {size} mm: the reading is more than 1 mm off.
problem.overhang: Overhang: not a step of the staircase.
problem.order: The clearances must grow from clamp to turn. Check the steps you picked.

check.title: Ready to print?
check.none: No problems found: the part fits the build volume, the walls are thick enough, nothing leans past the overhang angle.
check.basis: Checked after every change, as designed (standing on its lowest point), with the printer and material of this part. Supports, bridges and the orientation are up to the slicer.

finding.size: Too large for the build volume: {size} mm, the printer takes {bed} mm
finding.sizeLying: Too large for the build volume: {size} mm, the printer takes {bed} mm. Laid on another side it would fit.
finding.wallTooThin: Walls only {thickness} mm, thinner than the nozzle ({nozzle} mm): they do not print
finding.wallThin: Walls only {thickness} mm, at least {minimum} mm (two lines)
finding.overhang: {area} mm² lean beyond {limit}°: the slicer decides whether they need support
finding.contact: Only {area} mm² lie on the bed: may come loose or tip over
finding.separate: {bodies} touch but are separate bodies: the slicer lays each on the bed by itself. Combine them if they are one part.
finding.overlap: {a} and {b} overlap by {volume} mm³ – as separate parts they do not go together; combine them if they are one part
finding.tight: {a} and {b} come within {gap} mm without touching – under the push fit of {minimum} mm per side, they only go together with force
finding.blocked: {joint}: {a} and {b} touch at {at} – the joint does not reach its limit of {limit}
finding.posed: {joint} stands at {value}, not as designed – the part is exported and checked the way it stands

firstStart.title: Welcome to PartBuddy
firstStart.solidcraft: PartBuddy shows and changes your parts through SolidCraft, a free CAD program that runs in the background. PartBuddy looks for it on its own; if it is not installed, download it and look again.
firstStart.assistant: Choose the assistant you already pay for: Claude through your Claude Code, or ChatGPT with your plan. You can sign in later as well.
firstStart.print: Enter your printer and material once; the assistant designs for them. Save or skip this step.
firstStart.projects: Every project gets a folder of its own here, with the design, the conversation, versions and exports.

logoProblems.tooBig: The file is larger than 512 KB – a logo is usually much smaller; an embedded picture cannot be built.
logoProblems.unreadable: The file could not be read.
logoProblems.unsafe: The file holds scripts, embedded foreign content or references to other files – for safety PartBuddy does not read it.
logoProblems.tooComplex: The drawing nests too deeply or has too many shapes for a sketch.
logoProblems.empty: The drawing has neither filled areas nor lines. Text cannot be built – convert it to paths in the drawing program.

blocks.ready: Shown in the view – Build makes it

kinds.lip: Lip or groove for a lid

hint.tappedHole: A hole with SolidCraft's thread of this size, drilled with the tap drill.
hint.screwHole: Clearance after ISO 273 with room for the head after ISO 4762 or ISO 10642, plus 0.6 mm for printing.
hint.insertSeat: Typical values for ruthex inserts, one millimetre deeper than the insert. Check your insert's data sheet.
hint.boss: A boss with a seat for a heat-set insert of this size and at least 2 mm of wall.
hint.nutTrap: A hexagonal pocket after ISO 4032 with 0.3 mm of room and 0.4 mm of extra depth, with a clearance hole after ISO 273 below.
hint.slot: A slot as wide as the normal clearance hole, centred on the point, to adjust the screw.
hint.text: Text centred on the point, reading level. Engraved from 0.6 mm and embossed from 0.4 mm depth prints cleanly; letters from about 5 mm high.
hint.lip: For a shelled case: pick the face on the rim. The lip goes on the base, the groove with its gap into the lid.
hint.snapFit: A flexible arm with a catch, standing out of the face. Print it lying down so the layers run along the arm: standing upright it breaks along a layer. The other part needs an opening as deep as the catch.
hint.logo: An SVG file centred on the point, as wide as given. Filled areas and lines at their stroke width are built; turn text into paths first (in Inkscape: Path › Object to Path).

blocks.logoCentre: On the middle of the face
blocks.logoColours: A body per colour ({count} colours, multi-colour print)

logoColoursHint.deboss: The colours lie flush in a pocket of their shape; each colour is its own body for its filament.
logoColoursHint.emboss: The colours stand on the face; each colour is its own body for its filament.

blocks.moreHint: More blocks: tapped hole, nut trap, screw boss, slot, lip or groove for a lid, snap fit

tileHints.logo: Puts an SVG drawing on the face, raised or engraved
tileHints.text: Writes text on the face, raised or engraved
tileHints.screwHole: A hole for a screw with room for its head, also as a row
tileHints.insertSeat: A hole for a heat-set insert, also as a row

assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.suggested: Order proposed from the geometry: contact, bottom up, fasteners last

plate.title: Print plate
plate.switch: Show assembled or on the print plate
plate.tooTall: {part} is taller than the build height
